neutral_facts.value: The accused, a police constable, and his brother were involved in an incident where the accused's wife was found hanging in their home. The prosecution alleged that the accused and his brother murdered the wife, but the evidence did not directly link the accused to the act. Witnesses testified that they found the wife in a hanging posture and called for help, after which the accused and others arrived and cut the saree to bring down the body. The medical evidence did not conclusively establish the cause of death as homicidal hanging. The accused and his brother were acquitted by the trial court and the High Court, with the Supreme Court affirming their acquittal due to the lack of conclusive evidence linking the accused to the crime.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant, along with his brother, murdered his wife by strangulating her with a plastic rope and then hanging her from a hook. They claimed that the appellant had resigned from his police service to move to Saudi Arabia with an extra-marital partner, thereby deserting his wife and children, and that the circumstantial evidence supported the charge of murder.

quotes.text: The prosecution has imputed that in this heinous act, the co-accused his brother, who since has been acquitted, had assisted him.

The prosecution plea that the appellant had resigned from the service in the police department to move out to Jeddah/Saudi Arabia with the intention to perpetuate his illicit association with the lady thereat and that in a way he had deserted the deceased and the children, is also not borne out definitively by the materials on record.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the appellant was not present at the house when the deceased died, and that the medical evidence did not conclusively establish homicidal hanging. They also highlighted the acquittal of the co-accused and the lack of direct evidence linking the appellant to the crime, asserting that the prosecution's case was based on suspicion rather than proof.

quotes.text: The evidence of the witnesses when considered in conjunction with the testimony of the doctor does not link the appellant directly or indirectly with the actual act leading to the unnatural death of the deceased.

The fact that both the accused persons had been exonerated of the charge of cruelty under Section 498A IPC and that the co-accused, who allegedly had assisted the appellant in the perpetration of the crime had been fully acquitted by the courts below of all the charges also takes away the wind from the sails of the prosecution.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that suspicion cannot replace proof in criminal cases, and that the prosecution must establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The court emphasized that circumstantial evidence must be conclusive and leave no room for reasonable doubt in favor of the accused.

quotes.text: Suspicion however grave cannot take the place of proof - Prosecution in order to succeed on a criminal charge cannot afford to lodge its case in the realm of 'may be true' but has to essentially elevate it to the grade of 'must be true'.

In a criminal prosecution, the court has a duty to ensure that mere conjectures or suspicion do not take the place of legal proof and in a situation where a reasonable doubt is entertained in the backdrop of the evidence available, to prevent miscarriage of justice, benefit of doubt is to be extended to the accused.

The appeal is thus allowed and the conviction and sentence recorded by the courts below is hereby set aside.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The court considered the absence of direct evidence linking the appellant to the crime, the acquittal of the co-accused, and the lack of conclusive medical evidence supporting the prosecution's claim of homicidal hanging.

quotes.text: The fact that both the accused persons had been exonerated of the charge of cruelty under Section 498A IPC and that the co-accused, who allegedly had assisted the appellant in the perpetration of the crime had been fully acquitted by the courts below of all the charges also takes away the wind from the sails of the prosecution.
The absence of definite medical opinion about the homicidal death of the deceased is a serious set back to the prosecution.
